title: The router is honest, and it says the demonstration class is empty

two_errors_on_the_way.effect: REFUSE on all 130 tasks, including the 8 the executor wins
two_errors_on_the_way.law_applied: a gate that refuses everything is not a decision, it is a stub wearing a verdict

two_errors_on_the_way.error: two orthogonal questions collapsed into one verdict
two_errors_on_the_way.effect: 'can a skill be compiled?' answered REFUSE and was read as 'refuse the task'

the_measurement.interpretation: a literal in the goal is a near-perfect predictor of where this system can win. The two classes that need something OTHER than a literal are currently zero -- not because they are impossible, but because nothing here can name their target.

what_the_empty_class_means_for_the_thesi.claim: learn once, permanently, then solve everything
what_the_empty_class_means_for_the_thesi.status: the mechanism is real and measured (4/4 unseen goals at 2-4 ms on an addressable effect; 5/7 stable on form binding), but the class it serves is exactly the class that ALREADY has a literal. In this suite the demonstration-needing class is 7 tasks and the system wins 0 of them.
what_the_empty_class_means_for_the_thesi.the_honest_gap: a demonstration gives you a REPLAY of what was shown. Turning it into a capability that generalises to a predicate ('the shortest one' -> any instance) requires the ABILITY TO IDENTIFY the property, which is semantics, not procedure. A demonstration cannot supply semantics. That is the boundary, and it is not an implementation detail.
